lines.text: Do you know how a hot air balloon flies? There's no engine pushing it up. Just a fire, and physics.
When air heats up, its molecules speed up and spread apart. So a balloon full of hot air weighs less than the same space full of cool air.
The cooler, heavier air around it pushes it upward, just like water pushes up a cork.
To climb, the pilot fires the burner, heating the air inside to around a hundred degrees Celsius.
To come down, they let it cool, or pull open a vent at the top so hot air escapes.
There's no steering wheel. Winds blow different ways at different heights, so pilots steer by climbing or sinking into the wind they want.
The first people flew in one over Paris in 1783, more than a century before the first airplane.
So a balloon is just warm air, lifted by the cold air around it.
